Rashi on Yevamot 45b:10:1.english: He immersed her for the sake of a wife - For the sake of a niddah immersion, and not for the sake of a conversion immersion.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:10:2.hebrew: יכילנא לאכשורי בה - להיות גיורת גמורה. ואע"פ שלא טבלה לשם גירות, ואמר לקמן (יבמות דף מו:): לעולם אינו גר עד שימול ויטבול — דטבילת נדה סלקא לה לשם גירות, דעובדת כוכבים לא טבלה לנדותה:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:10:2.english: I am able to render her fit - [That is,] to be a full convert, even though she did not immerse for the sake of conversion, and [the Gemara] states later (Yevamot 46b): "One is never a convert until he is circumcised and immerses" — [nevertheless,] an immersion for niddah counts for her for the sake of conversion, since a gentile woman does not immerse for her niddah [impurity].

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:10:3.hebrew: ובברתה - ואע"ג דבת עבד הבא על בת ישראל היא — דהא נתגיירה זו וכבת ישראל היא — אפ"ה כשרה בתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:10:3.english: And her daughter - And even though she is the daughter of a slave who cohabited with an Israelite woman — since this [woman] converted and is like an Israelite woman — even so, her daughter is fit [to marry into the congregation].

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:11:1.hebrew: בה כדרב אסי - דאמר בשמעתין ההוא דהוו קרו ליה בר ארמייתא, שלא טבלה אמו לשם גירות, ואמר רב אסי: "מי לא טבלה לנדותה?" אלמא טבילת נדה סלקא לה לשם גירות:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:11:1.english: With regard to her, in accordance with [the opinion of] Rav Assi - Who said in our sugya [regarding] a certain [man] whom they used to call "the son of a gentile woman," because his mother had not immersed for the sake of conversion, and Rav Assi said: "Did she not immerse for her menstruation?" Thus [we see that] an immersion for menstruation counts for her for the sake of conversion.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:11:2.hebrew: ל"א לשם אנתתא - לשם אישות, וטבילת גירות הוה, אלא שאינה טבילה, דאמר בכיצד (לעיל יבמות דף כד:): אחד איש שנתגייר לשום אשה ואחד אשה שנתגיירה לשום איש — אינן גרים. יכילנא לאכשורי בה ע"י טבילות אחרות שטבלה אח"כ לנדותה. כך שמעתי. וקשיא לי: חדא, דקבעינן הלכתא התם הלכה כולן גרים; ואפי' למשנה ראשונה נמי, אי קמייתא לא סלקא לה, בתרא נמי לא סלקא לה, דלאו לשם שמים נתגיירה. ולשון ראשון עיקר ונראה בעיני:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:11:2.english: Another version: For the sake of a wife - [Meaning] for the sake of marriage, and it was an immersion for conversion, except that it is not [a valid] immersion, as it is stated in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad (above, Yevamot 24b): "Whether a man who converted for the sake of a woman or a woman who converted for the sake of a man, they are not converts." [Therefore,] I can validate her by means of other immersions that she immersed afterward for her menstruation. Thus I have heard. And this is difficult for me: first, because we establish the halakhah there [that] the halakhah is [that] all of them are converts; and even according to the first teaching as well, if the first [immersion] does not count for her, the later [immersion] also does not count for her, since she did not convert for the sake of Heaven. And the first version is primary and seems [correct] in my eyes.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:13:1.english: Son of an Aramean woman - Because his mother did not immerse when she converted.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:13:2.hebrew: מי לא טבלה לנדותה - ואותה טבילה עולה לה לטבילת גירות, דדת יהודית היא; וכן מי לא טבל לקריו:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:13:2.english: Didn't she immerse for her menstruation - And that immersion counts for her as an immersion for conversion, for it is Jewish practice; and likewise [with] "Didn't he immerse for his seminal emission?"

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:1:1.english: Who is he? Rav Yehuda - As [the Gemara] said [above]: "And even Rav Yehuda rules permissively regarding it."

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:1:2.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say - Regarding a half-slave who has intercourse with a Jewish woman.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:1:3.hebrew: הולד אין לו תקנה - בבת ישראל, כלומר ממזר הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:1:3.english: The offspring has no recourse - [To marry] a Jewish woman; that is to say, he is a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:2:1.english: When [it] was stated - That [statement] that he has no remedy.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:2:2.hebrew: כגון דקדיש - מי שחציו עבד וחציו בן חורין את בת ישראל, ואח"כ בא עליה, דכיון דקדשה הויא מקודשת לצד חירות אבל לא לצד עבדות, ונמצא צד עבד שבו משתמש בא"א. ולפיכך הולד ממזר, דכל הני דמכשרי בפנויה מכשרי, אבל באשת איש אפילו בישראל הולד ממזר, וכ"ש עובד כוכבים ועבד; אבל היכא דבא עליה בלא קדושין, כשר:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:2:2.english: Where he betrothed - [i.e.,] one who is half-slave and half-freeman [betrothed] a Jewish woman, and afterward had relations with her. For since he betrothed her, she is betrothed to the free side [of him], but not to the slave side, and thus it emerges that the slave side of him is engaging in relations with a married woman. And therefore the offspring is a mamzer, for all those [authorities] who declare [the offspring] fit [only] declare [it] fit in [the case of] an unmarried woman; whereas in [the case of] a married woman, even [if the father is] a Jew, the offspring is a mamzer, and all the more so [if he is] an idolater or a slave. However, where he had relations with her without betrothal, [the offspring] is fit.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:2:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> דנמצא צד עבדות שבו משתמש באשת איש:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:2:3.english: This is the reading: "that it emerges [that] the slave side of him is engaging in relations with a married woman."

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:3:1.hebrew: לדברי המכשיר - בעבד הבא על בת ישראל, מכשיר אפי' בא"א, וטעמא מפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:3:1.english: According to the statement of the one who renders [the child] fit - regarding a slave who has intercourse with a Jewish woman, he renders [the child] fit even in [the case of] a married woman, and [the Gemara] goes on to explain the reason.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:4:1.hebrew: אלא מאשת אב - דממזרות לגבה כתיב, דכתיב: "לא יקח איש את אשת אביו", וסמיך ליה "לא יבא ממזר" (דברים כ״ג:א׳):
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:4:1.english: Only from [one's] father's wife - For [the status of] mamzerut is written regarding her, as it is written: "A man shall not take his father's wife," and juxtaposed to it is: "A mamzer shall not enter" (Deuteronomy 23:1).

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:6:1.hebrew: כגון שבא על אשת איש - ומשום הכי הולד אין לו תקנה בבת ישראל, דנמצא צד חירות של עבד, כשבא עליה, משתמש באשת איש. ואע"ג דאי כולו עבד הולד כשר, כדאמרן, לדברי המכשיר מכשיר אפי' בא"א, הכא ממזר משום צד חירות, דהוי כשאר ישראל הבא על אשת איש, דהולד ממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:6:1.english: Where he engaged in intercourse with a married woman - And because of this, the child has no remedy [to marry] an Israelite woman, for it emerges that the free side of the slave, when he engages in intercourse with her, is engaging in relations with a married woman. And even though if he were completely a slave the child would be fit [of untainted lineage], as we said — [that] according to the one who deems [the child] fit, he deems [him] fit even [when born] from a married woman — here [the child] is a mamzer because of the free side, for he is like any other Israelite who engages in intercourse with a married woman, where the child is a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:7:2.english: There was an incident - [Involving] a full-fledged slave.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:7:3.hebrew: בין באשת איש - כדאמרן, שאין עושה ממזר אלא מי שיש לו קדושין על אחרים:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:7:3.english: Both in [the case of] a married woman - As we said [earlier], for only one who has [valid] betrothal with others produces a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:9:1.english: Rav Mari bar Rachel - He was [born] from an idolater who had relations with a Jewish woman.

Rashi on Yevamot 45b:9:2.hebrew: בפורסי דבבל - גבאים ממונים על ישראל. ואע"ג דגר בעלמא אסור למנותו פרנס על ישראל, דאמר מר כו', האי, כיון דאמו מישראל, "מקרב אחיך" קרינן ביה:
Rashi on Yevamot 45b:9:2.english: Among the pursei of Babylonia - [Tax] collectors appointed over Israel. And even though a convert in general is forbidden to be appointed as a leader over Israel, as the Master said, etc., [regarding] this one, since his mother is from Israel, we read regarding him, "from among your brethren."

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:10:1.hebrew: אטבלה לההיא עובדת כוכבים לשום אנתתא - שהיה רוצה לייחדה לו, והיה מטבילה כדרך כל בנות ישראל שטובלות משנתבעות לינשא. וטועה היה, דבעבד לא גזרו נשג"ז, כדאמרינן בנדה (דף כ):
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:10:1.english: He immersed that idolatress for the sake of [making her his] wife - For he wanted to designate her to himself, and he was immersing her in the manner of all Jewish women, who immerse once they are asked to marry. And he was mistaken, for regarding a slave they did not decree nashgaz [niddah, female slave, gentile woman, harlot], as we say in Niddah (20).

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:13:1.hebrew: מי לא טבלה לנדותה - תימה, דאמר לקמן (יבמות דף מו:) דגר צריך שלשה, דמשפט כתיב ביה; ואפילו למאן דאמר בריש סנהדרין (דף ג.) דבר תורה חד נמי כשר, מכל מקום אין דרך נשים להביא איש עמהן בשעת טבילה, ואשה אינה ראויה לדון, כדתנן (נדה דף מט:): "כל הכשר לדון כשר להעיד", ובהדיא איתא בירושלמי דיומא: "מעתה שאין אשה מעידה אינה דנה", ודבורה לא היתה דנה אלא מלמדת להן שידונו, אי נמי על פי הדיבור שאני. וי"ל: האי דבעינן שלשה היינו לקבלת המצות, אבל לא לטבילה; אף על גב דאמרינן לקמן (יבמות דף מז:) דשני ת"ח עומדים מבחוץ, היינו לכתחלה, דעדיף טפי. ויש מפרשים דכיון דידוע לכל שטבלה, כאילו עומדים שם דמי; ומיהו קשיא, דטבילת נדה בלילה, ולקמן (יבמות דף מו:) אמר: "אין מטבילין גר בלילה". אבל אי לאו כתיב "משפט" אלא אקבלת מצוה, אתי שפיר, והא דאין מטבילין היינו לכתחלה מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:13:1.english: Didn't she immerse for [purification from] her menstruation? - This is astonishing, for [the Gemara] states below (Yevamot 46b) that a convert requires three [judges], because "judgment" (mishpat) is written regarding it; and even according to the one who says at the beginning of Sanhedrin (3a) that by Torah law one [judge] is also valid, nevertheless it is not the custom of women to bring a man with them at the time of immersion, and a woman is not fit to judge, as we learned in a Mishnah (Niddah 49b): "Whoever is fit to judge is fit to testify," and it is explicitly [stated] in the Jerusalem Talmud of Yoma: "Therefore, since a woman does not testify, she does not judge," and Deborah did not judge [herself], rather she would teach them how to judge — or alternatively, [a case] by divine command is different. And one can answer: that which we require three [judges] is for the acceptance of the commandments, but not for the immersion; even though we say below (Yevamot 47b) that two Torah scholars stand outside, that is lekhatchilah, because it is preferable. And there are those who explain that since it is known to all that she immersed, it is considered as though they are standing there; however, this is difficult, for the immersion of a menstruant is at night, and below (Yevamot 46b) [the Gemara] says: "One does not immerse a convert at night." But if "judgment" is written only regarding the acceptance of the commandments, it works out well, and that which one does not immerse [a convert at night] is lekhatchilah by rabbinic decree.

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:2:1.hebrew: משום דאתי צד עבדות ומשתמש באשת איש - והא דמשמע בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ז. ושם) ד"התקדשי לחציי" לא אמר כלום, אי לאו משום ד"אי בעינן למינסב אחריתי נסיבנא" קאמר — היינו משום דשייר בקניינו, כדאמר בהשולח (גיטין דף מג. ושם); והכא לא שייר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:2:1.english: Because the slave side comes and engages in relations with a married woman - And as for that which is implied in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7a and there), that [saying] "Be betrothed to half of me" would have no effect were it not that he means "If I want to marry another [woman], I will marry [her]" — that is because [otherwise] he left something out in his acquisition, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaSholeach (Gittin 43a and there); whereas here, he did not leave anything out.

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:5:1.hebrew: מה אשת אב כו' - וא"ת: מה לאשת אב, שכן כרת ומיתה? ויש לומר: דממזרות תלוי בתפיסת קדושין, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:5:1.english: "Just like [one's] father's wife, etc." - And if you ask: What [comparison can be made] to one's father's wife, since [that union carries] karet and [judicial] death? And one can answer that mamzerut depends on whether betrothal takes effect, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:9:1.hebrew: רבא אכשריה לרב מרי בר רחל - רבא גרסי' ולא רב, דרב מרי בריה דאיסור גיורא הוה, שהיה בימי רבא, כדמוכח בפ' מי שמת (ב"ב קמט. ושם):
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:9:1.english: Rava ruled Rav Mari bar Rachel fit - We read "Rava" and not "Rav," because Rav Mari was the son of Issur Giora, who lived in the days of Rava, as is evident in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemeit (Bava Batra 149a, and there).

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:9:2.hebrew: פורסי דבבל - ממונה, כדאמר בפ"ק דיומא (דף ט.): "מאי פרהדרין? פורסי":
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:9:2.english: Pursei of Babylonia - [This means] an appointed official, as it says in the first chapter of Yoma (9a): "What is [the meaning of] parhedrin? Pursei."

Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:9:3.hebrew: כיון דאמו מישראל מקרב אחיך קרינן ביה - מכאן קשה לפי' הקונטרס, דפירש באלו נאמרין (סוטה דף מא. ושם) גבי אגריפס המלך, שאמרו לו "אחינו אתה", וקאמר בגמרא דבאותה שעה נתחייבו שונאיהם של ישראל כלייה שהחניפו לאגריפס; ופי' בקונטרס שקראוהו "אחינו" לפי שהיתה אמו מישראל. ולפירושו אמאי נענשו? הא אמרינן הכא: כיון דאמו מישראל — "מקרב אחיך" קרינן ביה! ואע"ג דתניא בתוספתא (דסנהדרין פ"ד) דאין מעמידין מלך אלא מן המשיאים לכהונה, מ"מ תימה הוא לומר דמשום איסורא דרבנן נתחייבו כלייה. ואומר רבינו שמואל, דהורדוס לא נשא בת ישראל שעשה תשובה, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דב"ב (דף ד.), ולכך נענשו; ואע"פ שהיה עבד, קראוהו "אחינו" לפי שהיה אחיהם במצות. ואתי שפיר הא דאמר שמואל בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין ע:): "כל דאמר מבית חשמונאי קאתינא — עבדא הוא"; ושמואל גופיה אית ליה (לעיל עמוד א) דעובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל — הולד כשר, אלא ודאי לא נשא ישראלית. וא"ת: מ"מ אמאי עבדא הוא? והלא מסתמא כשמלך הורדוס נתייאשו בעליו, ושמואל אית ליה (לקמן יבמות דף מח.): המפקיר עבדו יצא לחירות ואין צריך גט שחרור! וי"ל: דשמא היו מצפים שתהא גאותו מושפלת. וא"ת: דהכא משמע דגר שאין אמו מישראל אין כשר לדון, ובפ' אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לו: ושם) תנן: "הכל כשרים לדון", ופריך: "תנינא", ומשני: "חדא לאתויי גר וחדא לאתויי ממזר"; משמע דגר, אע"פ שאין אמו מישראל אלא שנתגייר בעצמו, דכשר לדון — דקרינן ליה "בא מטיפה פסולה", דקאמר התם: "אבל גר מטיפה פסולה — לא"! וי"ל: דהתם מיירי לדון גר חברו, כדאמר בפ' מצות חליצה (לקמן יבמות דף קב. ושם): גר דן את חברו דבר תורה, ואם היתה אמו מישראל — דן אפילו ישראל. וא"ת: בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין עו:) אמרינן: "מי שהוחזקו אבותיו משוטרי הרבים", למימרא דלא מוקמינן פסולים, ורמינהו: "הכל כשרים לדון כו'", ואמר רב יהודה: "לאתויי ממזר" — ומאי קושיא? דהתם היינו לדון את חברו! וי"ל: דממזר, כיון דאביו ואמו מישראל — "מקרב אחיך" קרינן ביה. תדע, דהא דרשינן: "עליך" הוא דבעינן "מקרב אחיך", וחברו ממזר מיקרי שפיר "עליך", שבא מזרע ישראל; ואי מיפסל ממזר לדון את ישראל, מיפסל נמי לחברו. ובפרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לו:) דקעביד צריכותא בין גר לממזר, אע"פ שגר וממזר חלוקין, דגר אינו דן אלא חברו, מ"מ נקט צריכותא לפי שהמשנה שנויה סתם, ואין חילוק זה מפורש בה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 45b:9:3.english: Since his mother is of Jewish [lineage], we call him "from among your brethren" - From here there is a difficulty with the commentary of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained in [the chapter] Elu Ne'emarin (Sotah 41a, and there [in the commentary]) regarding King Agrippa, to whom they said, "You are our brother," and the Gemara states that at that very moment the enemies of Israel [a euphemism for Israel] became liable to destruction because they flattered Agrippa; and the Kuntres [Rashi] explained that they called him "our brother" because his mother was of Jewish [lineage]. According to his explanation, why were they punished? Behold, we say here: since his mother is of Jewish [lineage], we call him "from among your brethren"! And even though it is taught in the Tosefta (Sanhedrin, ch. 4) that we appoint a king only from those who may marry [their daughters] into the priesthood, nevertheless it is astonishing to say that because of a rabbinic prohibition they became liable to destruction. And Rabbenu Shemuel [Rashbam] says that Herod did not marry a Jewish woman — [even though] he repented, as we say in the first chapter of Bava Batra (4a) — and therefore they were punished; and even though he was a slave, they called him "our brother" because he was their brother in [observing the] commandments. And this accords well with what Shmuel said in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 70b): "Anyone who says, 'I come from the House of the Hasmoneans' is a slave"; and Shmuel himself holds (above, 45a) that when a gentile or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is fit [of valid Jewish lineage] — rather, he certainly did not marry a Jewish woman. And if you ask: Nevertheless, why is he a slave? Presumably, when Herod became king, his masters despaired [of recovering him], and Shmuel holds (below, Yevamot 48a) [that] one who declares his slave ownerless — [the slave] goes free and does not require a bill of manumission! One can answer: Perhaps they were hoping that his pride would be humbled. And if you ask: Here it implies that a convert whose mother is not of Jewish [lineage] is not fit to judge, whereas in the chapter Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 36b, and there [in the commentary]) we learned [in the Mishnah]: "All are fit to judge," and [the Gemara] asks: "We already learned this," and answers: "One [serves] to include a convert, and one [serves] to include a mamzer" — which implies that a convert, even though his mother is not of Jewish [lineage] but rather he converted on his own, is fit to judge, since we apply to him [the description] "comes from an unfit drop," as it says there: "but a convert, [who comes] from an unfit drop, no"! One can answer: There it is speaking of judging his fellow convert, as it says in the chapter Mitzvat Chalitzah (below, Yevamot 102a, and there [in the commentary]): a convert judges his fellow [convert] by Torah law, and if his mother was of Jewish [lineage], he judges even an Israelite. And if you ask: In the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 76b), we say: "[Families] whose ancestors were established as public officers [are presumed fit]," which implies that we do not appoint disqualified persons [to public office], and [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: "All are fit to judge, etc.," and Rav Yehudah said: "[It comes] to include a mamzer" — now what is the difficulty [if] there [the Mishnah] refers to judging his fellow [mamzer]? One can answer: Regarding a mamzer, since both his father and his mother are of Jewish [lineage], we call him "from among your brethren." Know [that this is so], for we expound: it is [for] "over you" that we require "from among your brethren," and his fellow mamzer is properly called "over you," since he comes from Jewish seed; and if a mamzer were disqualified from judging an Israelite, he would also be disqualified [from judging] his fellow [mamzer]. And in the chapter Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 36b), where [the Gemara] makes a tzerichuta [an explanation of why both are needed] between a convert and a mamzer, even though a convert and a mamzer are different — in that a convert judges only his fellow [convert] — nevertheless it states a tzerichuta because the Mishnah is taught unspecifically, and this distinction is not stated explicitly in it.
